sections.content: How many people stayed in Waltham Cross after gaining qualifications?

Waltham Cross is a small town in the East of England. Waltham Cross does not have its own university.

Waltham Cross has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Waltham Cross ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 470 state-school pupils from Waltham Cross who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 125 (27%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 150 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Waltham Cross to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Waltham Cross' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Waltham Cross in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Waltham Cross' GCSE cohort:

  • 25 graduates left the East of England
  • 25 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East of England

In 2018 to 2019, 39% of graduates and 41% of qualified non-graduates living in Waltham Cross had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 140 graduates and 135 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Waltham Cross. This is compared with the 125 graduates and 150 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 57% of the graduates had also lived in Waltham Cross as GCSE pupils, while 39% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Waltham Cross in 2018 to 2019, 63% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 41% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
